findings.consequence: The r1 repair target named lines 33 (actually 31; the r1 report's citation was two lines high) and 187. Only 31 was repaired, and repairing it in isolation converted a consistent canon error into an on-page self-contradiction. The chapter now describes the same object twice and differently: at 31 the ledger's one non-measurement entry is a designation for the Stair, with 'third site confirmed on bearing' as the separate unfinished last line, which is exactly Book 7 (chapter-20.md:71, the designation 'near the page's top' beside the mark on the second stake; chapter-20.md:81, Karis: 'He says third. This is the second. The Ring's the first, by his stakes — thirty-one there, thirty-two here'); at 187, a hundred and fifty-six lines later, Karis herself tells the table the entry is 'for the third site'. It is Karis who is made wrong, in the one paragraph in the chapter whose entire persuasive force is that she is precise about what she does and does not know, and she is wrong about the object under her own hand while arguing that everything she cannot read points west. The downstream cost r1 named still stands: the index is carried into Ch17/Ch20 anchored to a site the surveyor never reached, and a designation for a site he never reached would not survive the decode against Vastin's records. Because the two statements are now in open conflict rather than quietly both wrong, a reader who is tracking the ledger will hit it, which lifts this above its r1 severity.
findings.repair_target: Line 187 only; line 31 is now correct and must not move. Bring Karis's clause into agreement with the inventory and with B7: the one entry that is not a measurement is a designation for the site the surveyor was standing in, and the ledger's unfinished last line is the one that names a third site on a bearing — e.g. 'The kit's ledger carried one entry that was not a measurement: a designation for the site he was standing in, in an index, in the surveyor's own hand'. Keep the rest of the sentence intact — she must still not know what the index is in, and 'because a man does not write index in his own field book for his own convenience' is the clause that earns the case. Do not add any reading of the index and do not let the third site's mention drift out of the unfinished-line register.

draft_evidence.quote: His term stands: spring, whatever's on that bearing, his crew comes. He said it at the plank and Pike wrote Noted, and a thing Pike writes is a thing.

findings.consequence: The F-006 repair delivers the missing plant and pays for it with a new contradiction against the scene it is remembering. Two facts are wrong in one clause. The word was Cael's, not Pike's — chapter-24.md:43-47 is Teague's term, then 'Noted,' Cael said, with Pike standing back from the sheet and not speaking. And Pike did not write anything: chapter-24.md:31 is the beat the whole of Book 7 Ch24 turns on — 'He put the pen down. He did not enter a line number. The five names stayed where they were, eleventh' — a board-keeper declining to write, in front of a room, because his ledger has no column for what the crew is. Book 8's own reconciliation decisions list 'Pike's nine lines and the blank season line' among the facts this book must not contradict, and this chapter has already honoured that at ch01.md:23 ('he did not say tenth, because the season line above it is still blank'), so the draft contradicts Book 7 and itself in the same file. The damage is compounded by register: the sentence is inside Cael's own log, so the narrator is made to misreport a word he himself spoke four days earlier, and the follow-on clause 'a thing Pike writes is a thing' rests the plant's authority on a piece of paper that does not exist. A reader coming off Book 7's close will hit it; the term is also the load-bearing plant for Ch17-21, so it should not be carried forward on a false record.

The placement is right — that table is the only room Oryn and Brom share in the chapter — but the six-word phrase repeats verbatim within a hundred words, which is audible. The r1 target's own suggestion, 'from her end of the table', avoids it. Line-edit item, not a defect.

ch01.md:7 now sources the inn's six to 'the hundred and two before the snow'. Book 7 stages the back room being taken on the first-snow day itself (chapter-24.md:65-69), not before it, so 'before the snow' is a day or two loose read strictly, and idiomatic read as 'before the winter set in'. The arithmetic — the part the finding was about — is exactly right. Flagged only so the state-ledger entry uses the day and not the phrase.

The F-002 repair widens the gap between the posted rate and the crew's rate: at 'a mark a head a week' five people would pay roughly a hundred and eight over five months, and they pay twenty. The scene earns it — Pike says the number, the innkeeper answers with his name, Pike answers with 'Eleventh' — and 'meadow rate' is doing the work of explaining why a room is priced like a tent. It reads as a favour bought with a board-keeper's word, which is the intended effect; noted because the size of the discount is now the largest unremarked number in the chapter.

The added Teague clause runs 'spring, whatever's on that bearing, his crew comes', which is his fixed sentence in indirect speech with the words 'whatever's on that bearing' intact. The r1 target asked that the fixed sentence not be restated verbatim. Converting to lowercase indirect third person is the standard way to honour that and I am not scoring it, but if the F-011 repair rewrites the sentence anyway, that is the moment to move further off the original wording.

F-008 was repaired one instance further than the target required: 183's 'And himself. Nineteen. Ten.' became 'And himself. Ten.' The catalogue still scans and it echoes Book 7's close ('and ten things held to nothing'), so nothing is lost that needs restoring. Recorded because the r1 report explicitly allowed 183 to stand and a later pass should not read its absence as a second defect.

Density is now 5,195 words against 4,600 (+12.9%), ninety-five words under the ceiling, and the two open HIGH repairs both replace rather than add. Ch2 should be planned at or under target so the book-level average does not start the run leaning on the band's upper half.
strengths: The fixed closing text survived the repair pass untouched and still compares byte-for-byte equal to the card, 'an index she can't read' included, with line 211 the file's last line of prose. Six of the eleven replacements landed within thirty lines of it and none of them drifted into it. Do not let the next pass touch line 211.

The money is now true at every step and sourced to Book 7 rather than asserted. 'four a month for the five of us, twenty for the five months' makes 4 x 5 = 20 checkable in the sentence that states it, and the inn's six is traced to the hundred and two that Book 7's own close takes down to ninety-six. The chapter's credibility device — money stated to the mark — is the thing that was broken at r1 and it is the thing that is fixed.

The kit's restored sentence at line 31 is better than the canon it restores. 'The pacing cord, knotted at the fives, twenty strides to a cord, and the cord's end-loops worn to the shine that a thing gets when one pair of hands has used it for a season' keeps B7's knotting, keeps the r1 draft's own new observation about the end-loops, and reads as one clause. The ledger's two facts are separated in the same breath, with 'the line that stops' preserving the surveyor's broken-off sentence as an image. This is the model for what the 187 repair should match.

The F-010 repair is one clause and it fires the whole plant: 'Hesk's note had said true to a hair, and it was, in every hand but mine.' The irony the plant was built on — the instrument-maker who guaranteed the edge, and the one pair of hands it will not read — is now legible without holding chapter-24.md:87 in mind, the note is recalled rather than quoted, and Hesk stays off the page until Ch14.

F-001's fix is the right beat in the right room. Oryn's first look at the bound shoulder now happens at the Lowmarch table, the first time she and Brom have been in one room since the fork, and 'since the binding', the 'still and forward' carriage and 'which meant she would' are all preserved — so Ch6's arming survives intact and the two-count at lines 57 and 73 is no longer contradicted a hundred and twenty lines after the reader was asked to hold it.

F-008's fix protects the closing text rather than merely counting. 'Me: ten; the still place; a cord that reads everyone else' hands the age to the fixed sentence three lines below it, so 'Nineteen.' in the card's text lands bare instead of arriving as a repeat, which is what the finding was actually about.

The Teague plant, attribution aside, is delivered exactly at the size the packet asked for: one sentence, in the log's register, attached to the glance already on the page, with Teague not brought on stage and none of his four named. The repair should change the second half of that sentence and keep the first.

Everything the r1 report protected is still there. The 'Five months and twenty days' arithmetic (ch01.md:89) against the bite on the ninety-sixth day; the release staged as Lira's act with the sling coming off by her own knot; 'ask first, every time' honoured in both directions with Cael declining a reading he could have taken; the anomaly deniable at four-paces-to-forty-two and his forty-one and a piece, three times; Karis's ruler sentence said twice and changed only by where she is looking; 'Nobody answered.' after her case; and Cleon withheld at 'There's a man there who is.' The repair pass sanded none of it away.
